title: The mansion-tax surcharge looks set to start at £2m, catching around 134,000 homes
summary: Ahead of the 28 October Budget, Accountancy Age reports the High Value Council Tax Surcharge will start at £2m rather than £1.5m, roughly halving the homes caught to about 134,000 and putting the focus on the £1.8m to £2.2m grey zone. Revenue has refreshed its CAT, CGT and VAT guidance after Budget 2027, the EU has updated its list of non-cooperative tax jurisdictions, the Treasury Committee has questioned FCA leadership on a whistleblower matter and Palantir, and Quilter has grown its bereavement team by half ahead of pension inheritance tax changes.

stories.headline: High Value Council Tax Surcharge: £2m threshold reportedly confirmed
body: Accountancy Age reports that the Chancellor has ruled out the lower £1.5m entry point for the High Value Council Tax Surcharge ahead of the 28 October Budget, with £2m now the confirmed starting point. The decision roughly halves the number of homes caught, from an estimated 271,000 at £1.5m to about 134,000 at £2m. The surcharge is reported at £2,500 to £7,500 a year by band, and applies to whole-dwelling value.
stories.meaning: Private client teams should focus on the £1.8m to £2.2m grey zone, around 73,600 properties per Knight Frank. Commission independent RICS valuations as evidence against automated VOA valuations, and build the surcharge into cash-flow and pension drawdown forecasts. Restructuring to avoid the charge is discouraged, since it could trigger CGT or SDLT.

charts.note: Moving the entry point to £2m roughly halves the number of dwellings in scope.

stories.headline: EU updates its list of non-cooperative tax jurisdictions
body: The Council of the EU has refreshed Annex I and Annex II of its list of non-cooperative tax jurisdictions. Practice teams should factor the update into disclosure, DAC6, and withholding analyses for Irish-headquartered groups and inbound structures.

stories.headline: Revenue refreshes CAT, CGT and VAT guidance after Budget 2027
body: Revenue has refreshed its capital acquisitions tax guidance to reflect Budget 2027 amendments, issued further capital gains tax manual amendments, and published a batch of VAT manual updates. Private client teams should re-check reliefs, thresholds, and valuation references before advising on lifetime transfers and estate planning, and indirect tax teams should review sector-specific supply treatment and place-of-supply points.
stories.meaning: Refresh client letters and planning templates now, ahead of year-end disposal activity. Guidance that changed after the Budget will catch out templates drafted before it.

stories.headline: European Parliament adopts recommendations on corporate tax strategy
body: MEPs have agreed a set of recommendations for the EU's future corporate tax strategy. The resolution is a direction-of-travel signal for multinational groups and advisers monitoring Pillar Two implementation and the direction of country-by-country reporting and ATAD-adjacent files.

stories.headline: Special Assignee Relief Programme statistics for 2024 published
body: Revenue's SARP statistics for 2024 are now available, a useful reference for inbound assignment planning and HR-tax advisory work for Irish-based multinational clients.

stories.headline: Revenue issues renewed scam warning
body: Irish Revenue has issued a renewed warning on phishing and impersonation scams aimed at taxpayers. Practices should remind clients that Revenue will not request bank details, PINs, or passwords by SMS, email, or phone.
stories.meaning: Send a one-paragraph client reminder this week. Fraud attempts spike around filing and Budget periods, and a firm that warns early protects both the client and its own reputation.

stories.headline: Dublin hosts the Tax Administration EU Summit
body: Dublin hosted the Tax Administration EU Summit, bringing together EU revenue authorities on cooperation, digitalisation, and compliance strategy. The summit is a backdrop to expected further moves on cross-border data exchange and real-time reporting alignment.

stories.headline: Half the UK population is struggling to keep up with announced tax changes
body: With two weeks to the Autumn Budget, speculation around the mansion tax, inheritance tax, and pensions tax is driving client enquiries. A Professional Adviser survey finds half of the UK population reports struggling to keep up with announced changes.

stories.headline: Plannr and Dynamic Planner launch two-way integration
body: Advice CRM Plannr has gone live with a two-way integration with cash-flow modelling tool Dynamic Planner, allowing advice firms to sync client fact-find, risk-profiling, and portfolio data without re-keying. Practical for IFA back-office teams running both platforms.

stories.headline: Wealth M&A outlook: £500m to £2bn AUA firms the next battleground
tags: Too big to bolt on, too small to lead
body: An opinion piece from Dyer Baade and Company argues that the next phase of UK wealth-sector consolidation will centre on firms with £500m to £2bn in assets under advice: too large to be bolt-ons, too small to lead their own roll-ups, and increasingly priced by PE-backed consolidators. Expect valuation pressure and more off-market processes in the mid-tier.
stories.meaning: Wealth firms in that band should be building an independent view of value now, rather than reacting to the first approach. Off-market processes reward the prepared.

stories.headline: Treasury Committee questions FCA leadership on whistleblower inquiry and Palantir
body: MPs have questioned FCA leaders over a whistleblower matter and the regulator's commercial relationship with data firm Palantir, a watch-point for firms tracking FCA governance credibility and data-handling practices.

stories.headline: Quilter boosts bereavement team by 50% ahead of pension IHT changes
body: Quilter has expanded its bereavement support function by half ahead of the rules bringing unused pension funds into the estate for inheritance tax, a signal of the operational preparation larger firms are putting in place for the change. Smaller advice firms should assess their own capacity to handle a likely rise in bereavement and estate-settlement work.

items.label: Growth in Quilter's bereavement support team

stories.headline: Foster Denovo pre-tax loss widens to £1.1m
body: National advice firm Foster Denovo has reported its pre-tax loss widening to £1.1m even as group revenue and headcount expanded, underlining the margin squeeze still weighing on consolidating advice groups.

stories.headline: Former Nexus IFA director pleads guilty to £2m fraud
body: A former Nexus IFA director and a colleague have pleaded guilty to a £2m fraud, a reminder for compliance teams on governance, segregation of duties, and client-money controls at smaller advice firms.

stories.headline: LPA-related financial misconduct complaints rising
body: Complaints involving financial misconduct linked to Lasting Powers of Attorney are rising. Advisers should document attorney engagement, verify authority, and watch for warning signs of coercion.

stories.headline: Pensions UK: reform should sit within a wider economic strategy
body: Pensions UK has called on government to anchor pensions reform in a broader economic plan, as the industry awaits Budget detail on tax relief, salary sacrifice, and the inheritance tax treatment of unused pension funds.

stories.headline: IFAC's Fast and Loose challenges the stance of Budget 2027
body: The Irish Fiscal Advisory Council has published Fast and Loose, setting out its concerns on the stance of Budget 2027, and the ESRI has released its post-Budget analysis covering distributional impact and fiscal stance. Both are likely to be cited by clients and in year-end economic commentary from Irish practices. Chartered Accountants Ireland has also re-circulated its Budget 2027 Special Tax Newsletter as a consolidated reference for tax teams preparing client communications and year-end planning.
stories.meaning: Clients reading the IFAC critique may ask whether Budget measures will hold. Have a view ready on which reliefs look durable and which could be revisited.
